name: Cafundo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only lexicon/sociolinguistic works (Andrade Filho 1993 wordlist; Fry & Vogt 1996 socling); no phonological description of the Cafundo cryptolect found.

sources.citation: Jon-And, Anna; Álvarez López, Laura. 2018 [online 2017]. A Cupópia do Cafundó: uma análise morfossintática. Revista de Estudos da Linguagem 26(1): 73-101. DOI 10.17851/2237-2083.26.1.73-101
sources.note: Nothing; purely morphosyntactic (copula omission, word order, NP/VP agreement) on a 1978 interview; no phonology, no stress/accent terms anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: Vogt, Carlos; Fry, Peter. 2005. As formas de expressão na 'língua' africana do Cafundó. Ciência e Cultura 57(2): 39-41 (stated to be a reworking of chapters of Vogt & Fry 1996).
sources.note: Nothing. Describes verbs (all 1st-conjugation -ar), periphrastic tenses, genitive compounding, homonymy; says mother tongue is regional Portuguese identifiable with the caipira dialect (Amaral 1976) and grammatical structures are borrowed from Portuguese (p.39). Word list uses Portuguese orthographic accents (cupópia, injó, nâni) but no prosodic comment.

sources.citation: Petter, Margarida Maria Taddoni. 1998. Línguas especiais, línguas secretas: na África e no Brasil. Revista da ANPOLL 4: 185-201. DOI 10.18309/anp.v1i4.287
sources.note: No stress statement. Sec. 2.2 (p.193-195) gives lexicon size and morphosyntactic traits (after Andrade Filho 1993:182-194); p.196: 'a sintaxe e a fonologia acompanham, com algumas alterações, o modelo da língua comum' (syntax and phonology follow, with some alterations, the model of the common language = Portuguese).

sources.citation: Fry, Peter; Vogt, Carlos; Gnerre, Maurizio. 1984. A comunidade do Cafundó. Mafambura e Caxapura: na encruzilhada da identidade. Cadernos de Estudos Lingüísticos 6: 111-128. DOI 10.20396/cel.v6i0.8636656
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic/anthropological; states speakers' mother tongue is regional (caipira) Portuguese and that the 'língua africana' is a Bantu (mainly Kimbundu) lexicon used with Portuguese morpho-syntactic structures (p.111-112, 121).

sources.citation: Vogt, Carlos; Fry, Peter. 1983. Ditos e feitos da falange africana do Cafundó e da calunga de Patrocínio (ou de como fazer falando). Revista de Antropologia 26: 65-92. DOI 10.11606/1678-9857.ra.1983.111043
sources.note: Nothing. Social-structure and speech-use study; only structural remark is that the grammatical structure supporting the lexicon is taken from Portuguese (genitive N+prep+N expressions, reduced persons/tenses, juxtaposition syntax).

sources.citation: Petter, Margarida. 1999. A linguagem do Cafundó: crioulo ou anticrioulo? In Klaus Zimmermann (ed.), Lenguas criollas de base lexical española y portuguesa (Bibliotheca Ibero-Americana 66), 101-115. Frankfurt am Main: Vervuert; Madrid: Iberoamericana.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Petter's fuller structural characterization of Cupópia (the 1998 ANPOLL paper is a shorter companion); may expand the 'fonologia acompanha o português' remark.
sources.venue: Lenguas criollas de base lexical española y portuguesa (Bibliotheca Ibero-Americana 66)
